subject.title: chore: resolve gollaw code health audit findings (#293)

question: Is this broad gollaw cleanup ready to merge as one PR after green checks and text-send proof, or should maintainers require more focused live media/sync/store-upgrade validation or split the branch first?
rationale: No concrete line-level defect remains from this pass, but the diff crosses message delivery, sync availability, and upgrade-sensitive store code, so automation cannot own the final compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Validate Representative Runtime Paths
options.body: Before merge, use maintainer testing or redacted proof for representative file, voice, status send, sync, backfill, and existing-store upgrade paths on the current head.

options.title: Accept Broad Refactor Risk
options.body: Maintainers may merge with the current green checks and sufficient text-send proof if they are comfortable owning the remaining unproven runtime surface.

options.title: Split If Confidence Drops
options.body: If focused review finds behavior drift, pause this branch and split the cleanup into narrower PRs around send, sync, and store changes.

recommendation.title: Validate Representative Runtime Paths
recommendation.body: Before merge, use maintainer testing or redacted proof for representative file, voice, status send, sync, backfill, and existing-store upgrade paths on the current head.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled current-main ownership across the central send, sync, store, and WA client areas affected by the merge-risk decision.
